A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ToolACE-MT, with matching authors, methods, benchmark experiments, and appendix prompts. Their complete text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on BFCL-v3, ACEBench, and τ-Bench, together with component ablations, scaling experiments, and generation-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds dialogue-quality measurements, public-dataset training comparisons, token and monetary costs, and verification-failure frequencies.

M1.justification: The initialization, alternating complexity injection and reasonability refinement, and rule/model verification procedures are retained. All eight generation prompts in Figures 8–15 are unchanged. The formal trajectory correction does not establish a change to the implemented generation procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds training on ToolACE-10k, an 8k sample from Toucan-1.5M, and ToolDial-9k for comparator models, including predominantly single-turn ToolACE data. Evaluation coverage remains BFCL-v3, ACEBench English, and the Retail/Airline domains of τ-Bench.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds models trained on ToolACE-10k, Toucan-1.5M, and ToolDial-9k as evaluated comparators across the three retained benchmarks. This substantially broadens the training-data comparison beyond the original MAS control; existing model comparators and ablations remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 introduces semantic similarity, entailment rate, entropy, and Distinct-3 for evaluating generated data. Efficiency measurement expands to input/output tokens and dollar costs, and the added comparator experiment specifies Toucan sampling. Existing main training settings and benchmark metrics are retained; Appendix A primarily discloses previously unstated tuning details.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic coverage through direct coherence/diversity assessment in Table 1 and categorized verification-failure analysis in Appendix E/Table 9. It also decomposes generation costs beyond API-call counts. The original component ablations, refinement scaling, backbone comparisons, and model-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added descriptive statistics and failure percentages extend results without changing uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: New results cover dialogue quality, three public-data baselines, token/USD costs, and failure frequencies. For example, Table 5 newly reports GPT-4o generation costs of $1,737 for MAS versus $1,380 for ToolACE-MT. Original benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, including ToolACE-MT's 40.25% BFCL multi-turn accuracy; Table 8's 40.3% is rounding.

T1.justification: The problem formulation changes the defined conversation endpoint from observation o^n to assistant action a^n. This corrects the definition to match the retained initialization expression and assistant-final-turn prompt. The POMDP assumptions and remaining mathematical formulation are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about non-autoregressive dialogue generation, scalable refinement, efficiency, data quality, and generalization across models. The new experiments support those existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking dialogue statistics to task efficiency, attributing monetary savings primarily to reduced input tokens, and identifying parameter handling as the main verification bottleneck. Appendix D discusses the single-turn disadvantage against ToolACE. Existing τ-Airline evaluation caveats and refinement/verification interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents hyperparameter search ranges, development-set selection, eight V100 GPUs, and LLaMA-Factory. Appendix D supplies access references for comparator datasets, and Section 4.4 states GPT-4o token prices. Previously reported final LoRA and optimization settings and all generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same research coverage. Appendix D extends positioning through references to and discussion of released ToolACE, Toucan, and ToolDial datasets, including their comparative strengths and weaknesses. Bibliographic formatting changes alone do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 introduces numbered section hierarchies and lettered appendices, makes local wording edits, explains the retained dialogue example, and adds an LLM writing-assistance disclosure. These are limited narrative changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column ICLR formatting, substantially rearranges Figures 2–3, and relocates/resizes existing figures and prompt boxes. It adds Tables 1, 6, 8, and 9 and expands the cost table with token and pricing columns. These constitute substantial visual and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The public-dataset comparisons, token/dollar accounting, quality and failure analyses, and additional implementation details strengthen the evidence and reproducibility of the existing work. These are useful extensions to an already extensive empirical study. A small drawback is Appendix D's claim of consistent multi-turn superiority despite Table 8 showing a 51.0% ACEBench tie with ToolACE; the net improvement remains positive but limited.
